question: We're moving our docs from Doc Detective 4 to 5. Our contributor guide teaches authors how to write tests, so it's full of ```` ```markdown ```` fenced blocks with sample `<!-- test ... -->` and `<!-- step ... -->` comments, plus ```` ```json ```` blocks of sample config. In v4 we had to wrap every one of those samples in `<!-- test ignore start -->` and `<!-- test ignore end -->`, or the sample tests ran and the JSON blocks turned into unsafe `runCode` steps. Do we still need all those wrappers in v5?

facts.text: No for the samples: Doc Detective 5 parses each file and doesn't read statements inside code blocks or inline code, so a sample test in a fenced block isn't run and doesn't need an ignore block.
A ```` ```json ```` block no longer becomes a `runCode` step; only blocks tagged `bash`, `python`, `py`, `javascript`, or `js` do.

must_not: Statements inside fenced code blocks still run in Doc Detective 5, so the ignore wrappers are still needed.
A ```` ```json ```` code block becomes an unsafe `runCode` step.
Each sample fence needs `testIgnore` in its info string to keep its statements from running.

wrong.answer: Yes. Doc Detective 5 still reads `<!-- step -->` comments wherever they appear, code blocks included, so keep each sample inside `<!-- test ignore start -->` and `<!-- test ignore end -->`. The JSON blocks are now plain text, so they no longer become `runCode` steps.

You can drop the wrappers. Doc Detective 5 doesn't read statements inside code blocks, so sample tests don't run, and JSON blocks no longer become `runCode` steps. To be safe during the move, run `npx doc-detective --input docs --ignore-code-blocks` once and compare the results.
You can drop the wrappers around the Markdown samples. Doc Detective 5 parses each file and doesn't read statements inside code blocks, so a sample test stays a sample.
